title: The Impact of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) on Online Usage Behavior
abstract: arXiv:2411.11589v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Privacy regulations aim to safeguard consumers, but can have unintended consequences on how users interact with websites. This article estimates the causal effect of the EU's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) on online usage behavior and decomposes it into usage frequency (unique visitors) and usage intensity (visits per unique visitor). Using a generalized synthetic control estimator across trillions of visits to 6,387 websites in 24 industries and 13 countries-11 months before and 19 months after enforcement-it compares observations subject to the GDPR (EU users or EU websites) with unaffected observations (non-EU users on non-EU websites). Weekly visits decline by 4.88% within 3 months and by 10.02%% after 18 months, with the decline increasingly driven by usage frequency: by 18 months, unique visitors decline by 6.61%, whereas visits per unique visitor decline by only 0.59%. translated_title: 《通用数据保护条例》(GDPR)对在线使用行为的影响
translated_abstract: 隐私法规旨在保护消费者，但可能对用户与网站的互动方式产生意想不到的后果。本文估算了欧盟《通用数据保护条例》(GDPR)对在线使用行为的因果效应，并将其分解为使用频率（独立访客数）和使用强度（每位独立访客的访问次数）。使用广义合成控制估计器，对24个行业、13个国家中6,387个网站的数十亿次访问（执行前11个月和执行后19个月）进行比较，将受GDPR约束的观察对象（欧盟用户或欧盟网站）与不受影响的观察对象（非欧盟网站上的非欧盟用户）进行对比。每周访问量在3个月内下降4.88%，18个月后下降10.02%，且下降日益由使用频率驱动：到18个月时，独立访客数下降6.61%，而每位独立访客的访问次数仅下降0.59%。平均值掩盖了相互抵消的效应。
tldr: 本文发现GDPR实施后在线使用行为显著下降，且主要由独立访客数减少驱动，而非每位访客的访问次数变化，揭示了隐私法规对用户行为的因果影响。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that GDPR implementation significantly reduces online usage, driven primarily by a decline in unique visitors rather than visits per visitor, revealing the causal impact of privacy regulations on user behavior.
